Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-07-31 | AAPL | Underweight | +1.4% | -2.1% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL: trim roughly 30% of the existing position, targeting ~60–65% of standard weight, but execute into strength rather than into the 300 support that was just absorbed on the heaviest volume in the window. Stage it — a 10–15% tranche at/above the 308–309 area now, the balance working as a sell-limit at 312.66 with a two-session soft time stop, and if AAPL trades below 305 before the limit fills, take 10–15% at the prevailing price rather than pretending to get 308.91. Retained core: daily close below 300.00 cuts to 50–55% of standard, below 294.38 to 40–50%, and a break of the 200-SMA at 277.96 triggers a full thesis reassessment. Do not pre-authorize a 284–278 falling-knife buy. No leverage, size for ATR 9.87 (3.20% of price), horizon 1–3 months re-underwritten at the next print.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk seats converge on the same direction — reduce AAPL — and disagree only on execution, which is the cleanest consensus in this record. What separates this from my five prior AAPL Underweights that lost money within five days (07-20 +3.2% raw, 07-21 +3.8%, 07-22 +3.8%, 07-23 +3.7%, and the 07-24 Hold at -7.2%) is that the trigger those lessons demanded has finally printed: a -7.35% close at 308.91 on 132.5M shares, ~2.6x the 50.8M average and the third-largest session in the data window, the first close below the 50-SMA (309.4994) since 06-30, the entire July leg round-tripped (07-02 breakout close 308.63), a MACD histogram flip to -1.3652, and price 5.35% below VWMA 326.39 and 5.60% below the 10-EMA 327.24 — a volume-weighted cohort now overhead. That is distribution on an earnings gap, not the sub-one-ATR momentum decay I incorrectly sold into four times in July.

The asymmetry is the second leg and the aggressive and conservative analysts agree on the arithmetic even while disagreeing on the label: ~+5.9% to the 324.37/326.39/327.24 confluence versus ~-10.0% to the rising 200-SMA at 277.96, with RSI 43.24 offering no oversold cushion (June's low was 32.20) and ATR at 9.87 having expanded from 8.06 two sessions earlier. Poor skew in both directions argues for shrinking, not for holding full size and hoping — which is why the neutral analyst's conclusion of "do nothing" is the weakest of the three positions.

The fundamental overlay caps the call at Underweight rather than Sell. The franchise is not broken: FQ3 revenue $109.4B +16.4%, gross margin 50.06%, operating margin 32.62%, diluted EPS +28.7%, nine-month FCF $110.2B, net cash $51.2B, and price still +11.14% above a rising 200-SMA. But the bull never sourced the 50.06% margin — the data has no segment disclosure to attribute +357bp to mix, pricing or a one-off — while management itself called memory pricing a "hundred-year flood," raw materials tripled to $7.6B and inventory rose 94% (to $11.1B), capex fell 28% flattering FCF, buybacks decelerated (~-12% YTD), the effective tax rate rose 219bp, and the September guide carried four headsets: supply, China softness, FX, and a softening Services line against structural App Store regulatory drag. Add an unmodeled CEO transition (Cook to Ternus) landing in a margin- and supply-constrained period, and the forward margin trajectory the market is repricing is a legitimate concern, not a headline.

Where I explicitly side against the analysts: (1) I reject the aggressive "bold contrarian convex trade" framing — this is risk reduction, not alpha generation, and a sell-limit is an execution tool, not a hedge; (2) I reject the conservative's 55–60% hard target and its 304.22 trigger, because 304.22 sits inside one ATR and no portfolio context exists — the trader's 60–65% expresses Underweight without abandoning an intact primary trend, and 300.00 is the correct structural trigger given the absorption of that low; (3) I reject both the aggressive's pre-authorized 284–278 catch and the conservative's rigid two-close 200-SMA gate as sole re-entry path — re-entry requires the 284–278 test plus a reclaim of 300–304 on improving momentum, or two sessions stabilizing above the 200-SMA plus that reclaim.

On re-risk timing I adopt the neutral's correction over the trader's, and it is the most important practical lesson from GOOGL (+11.4% against an Underweight whose re-entry gate sat 7–8% above spot): a daily close above 312.66 halts trimming and returns the stance to Hold, and 327.24 — not a distant gate — is the invalidation that permits a staged rebuild toward standard weight. What would change the call to Hold/Overweight: a daily close above 327.24 with the MACD histogram turning positive, or a next print holding gross margin ≥48% with an intact revenue guide and memory-cost offsets. What would move it toward Sell: a decisive close below 300.00 un-reclaimed, then 294.38, then failure of the 277.96 200-SMA. Stated gaps, not papered over: no segment-level margin attribution, no quantitative CEO-transition detail, no peer valuation comps beyond the ~34x annualized / ~37–38x normalized figures, and no holdings or cash data — so all sizing is a fraction of the caller's own AAPL weight, and the 289 target below is technical, not valuation-derived.

**Price Target**: 289.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months (re-underwritten at the next quarterly print)

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -2.1% (raw +1.4%) shows the Underweight’s absolute downside call was not confirmed, though the window is too short to judge a 1–3 month thesis. This supports the relative part of the thesis—AAPL lagged SPY—but undercuts the immediate distribution and 289-target premise, since price did not follow through lower after the 308.91 volume break. Next time, separate absolute Underweight from relative underweight and require a second confirmation—a close below 300 or continued SPY-relative weakness—before staging trims, rather than treating one high-volume down session as sufficient.

[2026-07-30 | AAPL | Underweight | -6.3% | -9.9% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Trim AAPL by roughly one-third of the position now (to ~65–67% of target weight), executed at or near the 2026-07-30 close rather than left to fill on limits at 338.2/340.1 above a 333.43 market — the FQ3 FY26 print lands after that close, so no session exists in which a rally can arrive; if AAPL is already below the 329.58 VWMA when the order works, execute at market. Keep the ~67% core: the 50SMA (309.30) and 200SMA (277.65) are rising and unbroken and the franchise is accelerating, so this is de-risking, not an exit. Treat 344.57 as a re-risk trigger, not a stop: rebuild to full weight on a close above 338.2 on >60M shares, confirmed above 344.5 on >55M shares with one follow-through session. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten post-print.

**Investment Thesis**: The debate resolved to reduce; the contested questions were size and whether to guarantee execution, and the neutral seat won both on arithmetic.

Direction: the bear's setup case is the stronger one at 333.43, and it is not the same argument that failed five times before. AAPL is +20.09% above the 200SMA (277.65) and +7.80% above the 50SMA (309.30); the MACD histogram has collapsed 81% (3.337 on 7/17 → 0.643) with ~0.53/session of cushion to a mechanical bearish crossover unless 336+ is reclaimed; RSI printed a lower high (68.90 at the higher 340.08 close vs 71.65 at 333.74); and the volume into the 344.57 record high is 51.9M → 56.1M on a reversal bar → 74.8M on a −1.41%/−5.09 gap-down day, the heaviest print since 7/02. That last item is where the aggressive seat was right and the conservative was too quick to call it noise: 74.8M on a down day is supply, not proximity to resistance. Forward pressure lands exactly where the print reports it — Qualcomm guiding Apple revenue declines to accelerate, supply-chain cost inflation with increases from September 1, Senate pressure on CXMT/YMTC sourcing, a failed ~$5T round number, buybacks down 25% y/y ($12.3B vs $25.9B), the tax rate reset to 17.5% from 15.0%, R&D +32.6%, an unexplained $12.8B intangible with a future $1–2B/yr amortization drag, and cash taxes down 35.6% (~$11B) flattering the FCF headline so that underlying CFO growth is ~30–35%, not 53%.

Prior lessons stated explicitly: five consecutive AAPL Underweights (7/20–7/23) each cost +3.2% to +3.8% of alpha inside five days because momentum decay was treated as a trigger inside a stacked rising trend. Three things differ now and one does not. Different: the binary event is tonight, so there is no window for the trend to reassert before the gap and dry powder has maximum option value; the distribution is an actual 74.8M-share supply print after a −5.09 open rather than decay in place of a break; and sizing is calibrated to the mapped −7.8% ladder, not 2×ATR. Not different: the trend remains fully stacked and rising — price above the 10EMA (331.31), 50SMA and 200SMA, VWMA (329.58) up eight straight sessions — which is why this is a one-third trim rather than the conservative's 40%+ and why it is Underweight, not Sell. No thesis-breaker was produced: revenue +16.6% in FQ2 ($111.2B vs $95.4B), gross margin +230bps to 49.3%, diluted EPS +21.8%, ~$78B of six-month free cash flow, net cash up ~$28B to $61.9B, debt down $13.9B, equity +44%. That is the core we keep.

Size: I adopt the neutral's correction over the trader's. A ~20% full target calibrated to a 2×ATR move (16.12 points, ~4.8%) does not honor the plan's own invalidation at 309.30 (−7.8%): a 33% trim leaves ~13.4% of equity exposed and a −7.8% event costs ~1.05% of equity, already over the 1% budget. So the trim is ~33–35%, not 25%. I reject the conservative's blanket 40% — beyond ~35% you only buy buffer for a tail that cannot be insured and overpay in the 35% bull branch — and I reject the aggressive's "cheap rebuild," since one cannot argue the stop is fake in a gap and then assume an orderly reclaim at 338.2, 1.4% above spot.

Execution: the trader's plan had a real defect that the conservative and neutral both caught — limits at 338.2/340.1 sit above a 333.43 close with the print hours away and may never fill, degrading the plan to carrying full weight into the event. So execute the trim now: limits at/above spot where possible, at market if AAPL is already below the 329.58 VWMA. On the other side I adopt their language correction — 344.57 is a re-risk trigger, with the real capital lines at 317.3 (2×ATR) and 309.30 structurally — but reject adding a discretionary "fresh portfolio risk review" gate on top of volume and follow-through conditions, which turns a defined trigger into a veto and manufactures the over-gating reinvestment risk the neutral warned about. Without portfolio context, sizing is expressed relative to the caller's own weight: at/above target, lean ~35%; materially over target or concentrated in tech, up to ~40%; already underweight, hold the core and add nothing into the event.

What would change the call: a close above 338.2 on >60M shares, confirmed above 344.5 on >55M with a follow-through session, rebuilds to full target. Post-print, redeploy in thirds only on a closing-basis hold of the 324.35–329.58 shelf, the final third uncommitted until 324.35 holds two sessions or 319.35 tags. A close below 324.35 cuts the tactical residual toward 319.35 and 309.30; below 309.30 invalidates the medium-term long. A sub-48.5% gross margin print alongside a soft guide converts this Underweight into a Sell. Missing and not papered over: no portfolio context, insider transactions explicitly UNAVAILABLE, social sentiment unavailable, news sample 20 of 108 records with zero coverage of July 23–28, BofA note headline-only, and no valuation multiple or consensus series — hence no price target.

**Price Target**: not provided

**Time Horizon**: 1–3 months tactical, re-underwritten at the FQ3 FY2026 print after the 2026-07-30 close

REFLECTION:
The −9.9% alpha (−6.3% raw) validates the Underweight in exactly the window it was written for — the post-print gap — though five sessions are too short to judge the 1–3 month "keep the ~67% core" half of the call. What the window supports is the supply read and the execution correction: the 74.8M-share distribution print was real, and forcing the trim at market rather than leaving limits at 338.2/340.1 above a 333.43 spot avoided a plan that would have carried full weight into the event. What it does not yet support is the de-risking-not-exit framing; the stacked 50/200SMA and accelerating franchise have bought nothing so far, and a sub-48.5% gross margin print would settle that leg. The lesson to codify: gate an Underweight on an actual volume-distribution print ahead of a binary event, not on momentum decay inside a stacked uptrend — that distinction is the entire difference between this call and the five prior ones that each bled 3.2–3.8% of alpha.

[2026-07-29 | AAPL | Underweight | -8.0% | -13.6% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Trim AAPL into strength: sell roughly one-third of the existing position into the $338–$345 area (today's $344.57 high caps the workable zone), initiate no new longs at $338.19, and do not short — the trend stack is fully intact and squeeze risk above $346.14 is real. Cap any residual at ~0.5x a normal AAPL allocation (0.3–0.4x if concentrated or a double-digit gap is intolerable), since ATR is $8.02 (2.37%) and the name already gapped −6.1% in one session. Manage on closes: above $346.14 on >60M shares halts further selling and forces reassessment (not an add-back trigger); below $319–$322.40 triggers another cut; below the 50-SMA at $308.59 clears the remaining tactical exposure. Horizon 1–3 months, fully re-underwritten at the 2026-07-30 print.

**Investment Thesis**: All three seats converge on reducing exposure (aggressive 0.5x with a re-entry mandate, conservative two-thirds sell, neutral one-third to one-half), so direction is settled and only size is contested; the neutral construction wins.

The decisive evidence is arithmetic the trader and neutral got right: $338.19 against the fundamentals report's own unverified ~$8.40 FY2026E midpoint EPS ($8.00–$8.80) is 38x–42x, and the $389 measured move the technical report derives requires 46x on that midpoint — a second re-rating, not earnings delivery, bought at a $5T market cap into a dated binary event. The bull case is real but already capitalized: H1 revenue +16.1%, Q2 gross margin 49.27%, FCF +63.5%, 1.15x cash conversion, ~$62B net cash, and a stacked rising structure (338.19 > 10-EMA 330.84 > 50-SMA 308.59 > 200-SMA 277.21, MACD histogram +1.17, no overhead supply above 344.57). But none of that is a floor — June 25 printed −6.1% on 107.0M shares and June 26 capitulated on 261.8M versus only 61–63M on the July breakout days, so the year's deepest liquidity sits on the sell side.

Durability is where the bull loses. Only two quarters are visible, FY2025 is unavailable in the cache, OpEx is outgrowing revenue, and the margin story depends on gross margin holding near record levels — the report's own linchpin, tested by the print. The Q2 buyback collapsed to $12.3B (−53% sequential and YoY), mechanically halving the share-count tailwind that manufactured EPS growth above net income growth. The $12.8B intangible build against ~$14.0B of noncurrent liabilities with no matching cash outflow is material and unexplained at this multiple, and the 17.46% ETR vs 15.00% prior (~$0.14/share H1 drag) may not be in consensus.

I reject both extremes. The aggressive analyst's "certain gain" plus pre-committed redeploy-at-more-size is relabeled market timing: if the print is good he buys back higher or not at all, and the $338.19 sale is the only certainty. The conservative's two-thirds default is too blunt against an intact rising stack, a de-risking balance sheet (~$61.9B net cash) and zero evidence of franchise deterioration — that is a portfolio-context call, not a blanket rule. A Sell/full exit and any naked short are unsupported: price is above every major average, %B ~0.83 leaves room to $346.14, and squeeze risk is real.

Prior lessons govern execution, not direction. The 2026-06-30, 07-01, 07-13, 07-20, 07-21 and 07-22 AAPL Underweights each cost +3.2% to +6.2% of five-day alpha by trimming an intact uptrend on momentum decay or nearby-level logic; the fix was to require a real trigger and shrink size rather than sell. This trim is different in kind — sized against a known dated event and a 38–42x multiple — but the lesson is why it stays at the light end, keeps a meaningful residual, refuses an automated add-back above $346.14, and does not chase a volume breakout. The 2026-07-22 AMZN lesson (weight divergence over the "trend intact, trim light" prior) is why this is not a Hold.

What would change it: a daily close above $346.14 on >60M shares halts the trim; post-print evidence of gross margin ≥48%, ETR ≤~17.5% reflected in consensus, Q3 buybacks above $20B and a benign explanation of the $12.8B intangible / ~$14B liability justifies a staged rebuild of part of the trimmed amount, deliberately not full size; a reset toward the ~$250–$270 valuation grid (≈30x on ~$8.40) materially improves the entry. Downgrades: a close below $319–$322.40 opens $308.59, and a decisive break of $308.59 voids the trend thesis. Explicit gaps, not green lights: no sentiment report, a one-day news sample (20 of 175 records, all 07-28, nothing 07-22 to 07-27), no insider data, an unverified forward EPS estimate, no FY2025 baseline, and no valuation multiples beyond the derived P/E; the caller's holdings and cash are unknown, so sizing is a fraction of their own AAPL weight.

**Price Target**: 320.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, through the 2026-07-30 print and re-underwritten post-print

REFLECTION:
The five-day window (−8.0% raw, −13.6% alpha vs SPY) validated the reduce direction but punished the residual: trimming into $338–$345 dodged part of the decline, yet holding ~0.5x still surrendered double-digit alpha against a rising tape, and five days is too short to judge the full 1–3 month thesis into the 07-30 print. What it supports is the core evidence — the 38–42x multiple on unverified ~$8.40 EPS, the read that the year's deepest liquidity (261.8M on June 26) sat on the sell side, and the $320 target, which price essentially reached. What it undercuts is only sizing: the neutral one-third-to-one-half compromise, chosen to honor the intact trend stack, was the cost center, and the conservative two-thirds would have preserved materially more.
